# Web Calculator — Specification

## Summary

A browser-based calculator that does basic arithmetic (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division) on whole and decimal numbers. It has a visible display, clear and backspace functions, keyboard input, user-selectable Light and Dark themes that persist between browser sessions, and a responsive layout that is usable down to a 320 px viewport width. The application runs entirely in the browser with no installation and no authentication.

## Implementation approach

The repository has no existing application code or package manifest. The calculator is built as a static web application using only HTML, CSS and plain JavaScript. It has no build step, adds no third-party packages and creates no package.json.

- `index.html` is the single page. It holds the display area, the button grid and the theme control, and loads the stylesheet and scripts through relative paths as classic (non-module) scripts. That way the page works both from a static file server and when opened directly from disk.
- `src/styles.css` holds the layout, the responsive rules, the Light and Dark theme styles (chosen by a `data-theme` attribute on the `<html>` element) and the hover and focus states for buttons.
- `src/calculator.js` holds the calculator state and arithmetic logic: digit and decimal entry, operators, equals, clear and backspace. It does not touch the DOM.
- `src/app.js` connects the logic to the DOM: button clicks, keyboard handling, display updates, and switching and saving the theme.

The selected theme is saved in `window.localStorage` under the key `calculator-theme` with the value `light` or `dark`. On page load, a saved value is applied to `document.documentElement` as the `data-theme` attribute.

Keyboard mapping: keys `0`–`9` enter digits; `.` enters a decimal point; `+` and `-` choose addition and subtraction; `*` chooses multiplication (×); `/` chooses division (÷); `Enter` does equals (=); `Backspace` does the backspace/delete function; `Escape` does clear (C).

## Conventions used in acceptance criteria

- "The display area shows the value X" means that the text content of the display area contains X, and the characters immediately before and after that occurrence of X, if any, are not digits, decimal points or minus signs.
- "A fresh page load" means index.html has just been loaded and no button has been clicked and no key pressed since.
- "With focus on the page document" means keyboard focus is on the document body or on any element of the calculator page, not on the browser address bar or another browser control.

## Declared artifacts

index.html
src/styles.css
src/calculator.js
src/app.js

## Acceptance criteria

- AC-001: Opening index.html from the local filesystem as a file:// URL in a current Chromium-based or Firefox browser, with no server process running, displays the calculator, and clicking 1, 2, +, 3, = in sequence results in the display area showing the value 15.
- AC-002: For each digit d from 0 through 9, after a fresh page load, clicking the button labelled 1 and then the button labelled d results in the display area showing the value formed by the digit 1 followed by d.
- AC-003: The page shows operator buttons labelled +, -, × and ÷, a decimal point button labelled ., an equals button labelled =, a clear button labelled C, and a backspace/delete button.
- AC-004: After a fresh page load, clicking the buttons 1, 2 in sequence results in the display area showing the value 12.
- AC-005: After a fresh page load, clicking 1, 2, +, 3, = in sequence results in the display area showing the value 15.
- AC-006: After a fresh page load, clicking 7, -, 1, 0, = in sequence results in the display area showing the value -3.
- AC-007: After a fresh page load, clicking 6, ×, 7, = in sequence results in the display area showing the value 42.
- AC-008: After a fresh page load, clicking 8, ÷, 2, = in sequence results in the display area showing the value 4.
- AC-009: After a fresh page load, clicking 1, ., 5, +, 2, ., 2, 5, = in sequence results in the display area showing the value 3.75.
- AC-011: After a fresh page load, clicking 5, +, 3 and then C results in the display area showing exactly the same text it showed on the fresh page load, and then clicking 2, +, 2, = results in the display area showing the value 4.
- AC-012: After a fresh page load, clicking 1, 2, 3 and then the backspace/delete button results in the display area showing the value 12 and its text not containing 123.
- AC-013: After a fresh page load, with focus on the page document, pressing the keyboard keys 9, *, 3, Enter in sequence results in the display area showing the value 27.
- AC-014: After a fresh page load, with focus on the page document, pressing the keyboard keys 2, +, 3, Enter in sequence results in the display area showing the value 5.
- AC-015: After a fresh page load, with focus on the page document, pressing the keyboard keys 8, /, 4, Enter in sequence results in the display area showing the value 2.
- AC-016: After a fresh page load, with focus on the page document, pressing the keyboard keys 4, ., 5 and then Backspace results in the display area text containing 4. and not containing 4.5.
- AC-017: After a fresh page load, with focus on the page document, pressing the keyboard keys 5, +, 3 and then Escape results in the display area showing exactly the same text it showed on the fresh page load.
- AC-018: The page shows a theme control. After it is activated once, the data-theme attribute of the html element is either light or dark. Each further activation changes the attribute to the other of those two values, and the computed background-color of the body element when data-theme is light differs from its computed background-color when data-theme is dark.
- AC-019: After the theme control is used to set the html element's data-theme attribute to dark and the page is closed and reopened in the same browser profile, the html element has data-theme="dark" before any user interaction with the reopened page.
- AC-020: After the theme control is used to set the html element's data-theme attribute to light and the page is closed and reopened in the same browser profile, the html element has data-theme="light" before any user interaction with the reopened page.
- AC-021: At a viewport size of 320×568 CSS pixels, document.documentElement.scrollWidth is at most 320, and the bounding rectangles of every calculator button, the display area and the theme control lie fully within the horizontal range 0 to 320 CSS pixels.
- AC-022: For every calculator button and the theme control, in both the light and dark themes, the computed value of at least one of background-color, color, outline-style, outline-color, border-color or box-shadow differs between the default state and the mouse-hover state, and at least one of them differs between the default state and the state after the element receives focus via the Tab key.
- AC-023: Loading index.html shows the calculator without any login, sign-up or credential prompt, and every criterion above passes without the user entering any credential.
- AC-024: After a fresh page load, with focus on the page document, pressing the keyboard keys 9, -, 4, Enter in sequence results in the display area showing the value 5.

## Open decisions

- OD-001 (high): When a calculation has more than one operator (for example 2 + 3 × 4 =), should the calculator use standard operator precedence (result 14) or evaluate each operator immediately in entry order (result 20), and what does pressing a second operator straight after another operator do?
- OD-002 (medium): Under what network conditions (bandwidth, latency, cache state) and with what measurement point (for example the load event) is the NFR-001 requirement to load within 2 seconds on a typical broadband connection checked?
- OD-003 (medium): What minimum text contrast ratio (for example WCAG 2.x AA, 4.5:1 for normal text) counts as sufficient contrast under NFR-004 in the Light and Dark themes?
- OD-004 (low): Which viewport sizes represent tablet and desktop screens for checking that the RQ-015 responsive layout functions correctly at those sizes?

## Out of scope

- Scientific calculations, graphing, user accounts, and calculation history synchronization across devices, as the design excludes them.
- The goals that the interface be intuitive, the experience fast and responsive, and accessibility and usability standards met in general have no objective check in the design. They are guidance for implementation and are not acceptance criteria beyond the specific checks above.
- Visual styling, colour palette and typographic choices for each theme, beyond the measurable checks above.

# Web Calculator — Implementation Plan

## Context

The repository has no application code and no package manifest. The calculator is a static page built from HTML, CSS and plain JavaScript loaded as classic (non-module) scripts through relative paths. There is no build step, no third-party package and no package.json, so nothing is generated in the checkout. The page works from a static server and from a file:// URL.

Provisional choice for OD-001 (open, high): operators are evaluated in entry order (2 + 3 × 4 = gives 20). Pressing a second operator straight after another operator replaces the pending operator. No acceptance criterion uses more than one operator, so a different resolution of OD-001 changes only the `chooseOperator` logic in src/calculator.js. OD-002, OD-003 and OD-004 add no work beyond the measurable criteria. The themes still use clearly contrasting text and background colours.

## Tasks

- Create index.html as the single page: `<!DOCTYPE html>`, `<html lang="en">` with no hard-coded data-theme, `<meta charset="utf-8">`, `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">`, a title, and `<link rel="stylesheet" href="src/styles.css">` (relative path). No form, login, sign-up or credential markup.
- In index.html, add a calculator container. It holds a theme control: a `<button type="button" id="theme-toggle">` with visible text and an aria-label, placed outside the button grid. It also holds a display element (`id="display"`, `role="status"`, `aria-live="polite"`) whose initial text is `0`.
- In index.html, add the button grid (`id="keys"`) as `<button type="button">` elements, each carrying a data attribute for its action. Digit buttons are labelled 0 to 9 (`data-digit="0"` to `data-digit="9"`). The decimal button is labelled . (`data-action="decimal"`). Operator buttons are labelled +, -, × and ÷ (`data-operator` values `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`). The equals button is labelled = (`data-action="equals"`). The clear button is labelled C (`data-action="clear"`). The backspace/delete button is labelled ⌫ with `aria-label="Backspace"` (`data-action="backspace"`).
- At the end of the body in index.html, load `<script src="src/calculator.js"></script>` and then `<script src="src/app.js"></script>` as classic scripts with relative src paths and no `type="module"`.
- Create src/calculator.js as DOM-free logic in an IIFE. It exposes a global `Calculator` factory, and also `module.exports` when `typeof module !== "undefined"`. State: the current entry as a string (initially `"0"`), a stored operand, a pending operator, and a flag for whether the next digit starts a new entry.
- In src/calculator.js, implement `inputDigit(d)`. A lone leading `0` is replaced (so 1 then 2 gives `12`). After an operator, equals or an error, a digit starts a new entry. Also implement `inputDecimal()`: it adds `.` at most once per entry and starts the entry as `0.` when it is fresh. The current entry is kept as a string so that a trailing decimal point such as `4.` is preserved.
- In src/calculator.js, implement `chooseOperator(op)` for `+`, `-`, `*` and `/`. If an operator is pending and a new operand has been entered, compute the pending result first and show it (entry order). If the operator is pressed straight after another operator, replace the pending operator. If it is pressed after equals, continue from the shown result. Also implement `equals()`: it applies the pending operator to the stored and current operands, shows the result and clears the pending operator. Equals with no pending operator does nothing.
- In src/calculator.js, format results to avoid binary floating-point artefacts: round to 12 significant digits with `toPrecision(12)`, then `parseFloat`, then `String`. This makes 1.5 + 2.25 give `3.75`, 7 - 10 give `-3`, 8 ÷ 2 give `4`, 9 × 3 give `27` and 9 - 4 give `5`. Division by zero shows `Error`, and the next digit or clear starts fresh.
- In src/calculator.js, implement `clear()`, which resets all state to exactly the fresh-load state with display text `0`. Implement `backspace()`: it removes the last character of the current entry being typed (123 gives `12`, 4.5 gives `4.`) and falls back to `0` when the entry becomes empty or is just `-`. After equals or an error it leaves the shown value unchanged, and the next digit starts a new entry. Implement `getDisplay()`, which returns the current display string.
- Create src/app.js to wire the DOM. On load, create a Calculator instance and immediately write `getDisplay()` into the display element's textContent, so the fresh-load text matches the text after a clear. Add one delegated click listener on the `#keys` grid. It maps `data-digit`, `data-operator` and `data-action` to the matching calculator method and ignores clicks outside a button. After every action, write `getDisplay()` into the display's textContent.
- In src/app.js, add a document-level keydown handler that matches `event.key`. Keys `0` to `9` enter digits. `.` enters a decimal point. `+` and `-` choose addition and subtraction. `*` chooses multiplication. `/` chooses division. `Enter` does equals. `Backspace` does backspace. `Escape` does clear. Shift is allowed, so that Shift-typed `+` and `*` work. Events with ctrlKey, metaKey or altKey are ignored. Call preventDefault for handled keys so that `/` does not open Firefox quick find, and so that `Enter` does not also activate a focused button and run the action twice. Update the display after each handled key.
- In src/app.js, implement theme handling. When the script runs, before any user interaction, read `localStorage.getItem("calculator-theme")` inside try/catch; if the value is `"light"` or `"dark"`, set it as `document.documentElement.dataset.theme`. When the theme control (`#theme-toggle`, its own click listener) is clicked, set data-theme to `"light"` if it is currently `"dark"`, otherwise to `"dark"`, so a missing attribute counts as light. Then save the new value under `"calculator-theme"` inside try/catch and update the control's visible label, aria-label and aria-pressed.
- Create src/styles.css with Light and Dark theme custom properties. Put the light values on `:root, html[data-theme="light"]` and the dark values on `html[data-theme="dark"]`. The properties cover page background, text, display, digit button, operator button, equals button, clear and backspace buttons, theme control, matching hover colours, and the focus-ring colour. Apply the page background and text colour to `body` so that its computed background-color differs between the two themes.
- In src/styles.css, add a responsive layout. Use `box-sizing: border-box` on all elements and `margin: 0` on body. Set the calculator container to `width: 100%` with `max-width: 360px`, small horizontal padding and auto margins. Use a 4-column CSS grid of buttons with `minmax(0, 1fr)` columns and a small gap. Give the display right alignment and `overflow-wrap: anywhere`. Give the theme control `max-width: 100%` inside the container. At 320 px width, no element extends past 320 CSS pixels and `scrollWidth` stays at most 320.
- In src/styles.css, add interaction states for every calculator button and the theme control. The default rule declares `outline: none` and `box-shadow: none`, plus `cursor: pointer` and a minimum height of about 44px. For each button class (digit, operator, equals, clear/backspace and the theme control), `:hover` sets background-color to that class's theme-specific hover variable. Each hover value must differ from the class's default value in both the light and dark themes. `:focus-visible` sets `outline: 3px solid var(--focus-ring)` with an outline-offset and a matching box-shadow, so that focusing via the Tab key changes outline-style, outline-color and box-shadow from the default state in both themes.
